incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT: spike in 5xx errors for /v1/generate in us-west1. Alerting on-call (olivia-oncall) and paging policy: high-error-rate.

olivia-oncall: on it. I see 5xx rate jump ~06:12 UTC, p95 latency up ~400ms. pulling logs from serving cluster now.

matt-eng: thanks for taking. if it looks like model-serving, flag me — I can assist with rollbacks.

olivia-oncall: quick check: dedicated customers look fine, appears to be traffic hitting hosted pool in us-west1 only.

incident-bot: Paging note: incident severity = SEV2 (partial outage), routed to #oncall + #customer-success.

olivia-oncall: found repeated OOM in worker process on node inference-usw1-4, stack shows KV cache growth and GC thrash. logs snippet: ```ERROR: runtime: out of memory
model: gptx-13b-quant, kv_cache_size=~1.2GiB```

elaine-cs: tagging for customer impact — which customers hit the hosted endpoint? any high-traffic clients affected?

olivia-oncall: list of clients in access logs: brightapps corp (requests failing ~1.2k req/min), internal integration tests, some trial accounts. Dedicated customers on reserved pools show no errors.

zoe-account: flagged BrightApps immediately. I’ll prep a short customer note — want to confirm scope before sending.

matt-eng: mitigation idea: enable temporary prefix-KV cache eviction and roll out emergency restart for affected pod group. prepping kubectl rollout restart for deployment/inference-hosted-usw1.

olivia-oncall: go for it. rolling restart now. command: ```kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/inference-hosted-usw1 --timeout=120s```

incident-bot: Action taken: rollout restart started by matt-eng at 06:25 UTC. Will monitor error rate.

olivia-oncall: error rate dropping, 5xx back to baseline in ~2 minutes. latency normalizing.

elaine-cs: draft customer message for BrightApps (please review):
"Hi BrightApps — We experienced elevated 5xx errors impacting the Generative API in US-West for ~06:12–06:27 UTC. We mitigated with a restart; most traffic recovered within ~5 minutes. We’re investigating root cause and will follow up with an RCA and remediation plan. Apologies for the disruption"

zoe-account: +1, clear and concise. Can we add whether dedicated pools were impacted? their account is on hosted only.

elaine-cs: added line: "Dedicated/reserved deployments were not impacted."

olivia-oncall: preparing status page update (draft):
"Status: Partial outage — Generative API (US-West)
Impact: Some hosted API requests returning 5xx and elevated latency between 06:12–06:27 UTC.
Mitigation: Restarted affected worker group; traffic returned to normal. Dedicated/reserved deployments unaffected.
Next update: We will follow up with a post-incident summary and timeline"

matt-eng: fine to post once we confirm final timestamps.

incident-bot: Incident marked RESOLVED at 06:27 UTC by olivia-oncall. Root cause investigation in progress.

--- (post-incident follow-up, later same day) ---

tomasz-sre: RCA draft: root cause = memory leak in KV cache path that manifested with new kernel selection change pushed during last week's model optimization rollout. The leak caused worker OOMs under real traffic patterns; autoscaler didn't spin new pods quickly enough because threshold set too high.

RCA timeline (summary):
- 06:11 UTC: first error anomalies observed in internal metrics
- 06:12 UTC: incident-bot auto-alert, on-call paged
- 06:13–06:24 UTC: investigation, confirmed OOMs in inference-hosted-usw1 pods
- 06:25 UTC: emergency rollout restart initiated (matt-eng)
- 06:27 UTC: error rate back to baseline; incident resolved

Root cause detail: the recent kernel selection tweak (commit abc123) introduced an allocation pattern that prevents timely KV cache eviction when memory pressure spikes. Under sustained traffic, cache grew >1GiB and triggered runtime OOMs. Autoscaler policy used average CPU-based thresholds and didn't react to memory pressure.

Corrective actions (short-term):
- revert kernel-selection change from commit abc123 in serving runtime (done)
- increase pod memory limit from 2Gi -> 3Gi for hosted pool in us-west1 (done)
- add emergency eviction toggle to pressure-evict KV cache remotely (implemented)

Preventative (long-term):
- add memory-growth alert (prometheus) on kv_cache_size per pod (P1)
- change autoscaler to consider memory and RSS (P1)
- add a regression test for kernel selection changes that simulates high-concurrency prefix workloads (P2)
- scheduled code patch to fix allocation pattern in kv cache (P1, assigned to matt-eng)

matt-eng: confirm revert PR merged and rollout validated. patch PR #4527 created to fix allocation pattern.

sanjay-ps: customer impact summary for billing: estimate outage window 15 minutes, ~1.2k failed requests/min for BrightApps, recommend 10% credit for that hour.

zoe-account: agreed on 10% credit and an offer for 1:1 sync to review reliability improvements. I’ll send the customer email once @elaine-cs finalizes.

elaine-cs: final customer follow-up (to BrightApps):
"Hi — thanks again for flagging. We had a short partial outage 06:12–06:27 UTC due to an internal memory issue. We’ve reverted the change, increased pod memory in the hosted pool, and added monitoring to prevent recurrence. We’ll issue a 10% service credit for the affected hour and are available to discuss next steps. Full RCA: [link to internal postmortem]."

olivia-oncall: small clarification on timeline: the auto-alert triggered at 06:12:07 UTC, restart completed at 06:26:54 UTC (logs). Please use these exact timestamps in the postmortem.

tomasz-sre: noted and updated RCA doc.

elaine-cs: posting status page update now with resolved state and link to RCA draft. customer email going out in 30m after legal/ops quick review.

zoe-account: sending notice to BrightApps now, cc'ing their technical lead.

matt-eng: follow-ups for eng: #1 finish allocation-pattern fix PR, #2 add mem alerts + autoscaler change, #3 run chaos test to validate host-level OOM handling. I’ll own 1 and 3.

sanjay-ps: finance approved 10% credit. please add note in billing system referencing incident ID INC-234567.

elaine-cs: closing thread when customer ack received. thanks everyone for fast mitigation. :heart:
